title: Dynamic Workflows
one_liner: A dynamic workflow is a script Claude writes to run many subagents in the background. The script, not Claude, holds the plan and the intermediate results.

core.title: The script holds the plan
core.body: With subagents, skills and agent teams, Claude decides each next step. In a workflow, a JavaScript script does: loops, branching and intermediate results live in script variables, and only the final answer reaches Claude's context.
core.why: Large jobs no longer fill the context window, and the orchestration can be read and rerun.

quotes.text: The difference is who holds the plan
quotes.label: Workflows > When to use a workflow

quotes.text: A workflow script holds the loop, the branching, and the intermediate results itself, so Claude's context holds only the final answer.
quotes.label: Workflows > When to use a workflow

core.title: Use one for scale or cross-checking
core.body: Suited to codebase-wide audits, large migrations, research with sources checked against each other, and plans drafted from several angles. Agents can review each other's findings before reporting.
core.why: For a few delegated tasks, plain subagents are cheaper and simpler.

quotes.text: Claude writes the script for the task you describe, and a runtime executes it in the background while your session stays responsive.
quotes.label: Workflows

core.title: Start one with a keyword or a bundled command
core.body: Include `ultracode` in your prompt, or ask in plain words ('use a workflow'). `/deep-research <question>` is the bundled example. `/effort ultracode` makes Claude plan a workflow for every substantive task.
core.why: The keyword only changes how work is structured; permission checks still apply.

quotes.text: include the keyword `ultracode` in your prompt
quotes.label: Workflows > Ask for a workflow

quotes.text: Run `/deep-research` with a question you want investigated.
quotes.label: Workflows > Run a bundled workflow

core.title: Runs are autonomous and bounded
core.body: No user input mid-run. Up to 16 concurrent agents by default and 1,000 agents per run. The script has no direct filesystem or shell access; its agents do the work. Watch and stop runs in `/workflows`.
core.why: If you need sign-off between stages, run each stage as its own workflow.

core.title: Cost scales with agent count
core.body: A run can use far more tokens than doing the task in conversation. Test on a small slice first. A `Large workflow` warning appears above 25 agents or 1.5 million projected tokens.
core.why: Usage and rate limits apply to every agent in the run.

quotes.text: a single run can use meaningfully more tokens than working through the same task in conversation
quotes.label: Workflows > Cost

quotes.text: run the workflow on a small slice first
quotes.label: Workflows > Cost

core.title: Save a good run as a command
core.body: In `/workflows`, select a run and press `s`. Save to `.claude/workflows/` (shared with the repository) or `~/.claude/workflows/` (personal). On a name clash, the project workflow runs.
core.why: A repeated process, such as a branch review, then runs the same orchestration every time.

quotes.text: The workflow runs as `/<name>` in future sessions from either location.
quotes.label: Workflows > Save for reuse

practice.title: Run the bundled workflow
practice.goal: See phases, agents and a single report.
steps: Run `/deep-research What changed in the Node.js permission model between v20 and v22?`
Run `/workflows` and open the run to view phases
practice.check: A cited report appears in your session at the end, not a turn-by-turn transcript.
practice.variation: Ask a narrower question and compare agent counts in `/workflows`.

practice.title: Commission a small workflow
practice.goal: Have Claude write and run a script on a small slice.
steps: Prompt: `ultracode: audit every file under src/routes/ for missing auth checks` (limit to one directory)
Choose **View raw script** at the approval prompt and read it
Approve and watch token usage in `/workflows`
practice.check: You can point to the loop in the script and the per-agent token counts.
practice.variation: Save the run with `s` and rerun it as `/<name>`.

gotchas: On Pro, workflows must be turned on in `/config` first.
The `ultracode` keyword is ignored in `-p` prompts and scheduled tasks; it opts in only when you type it.
A `Large workflow` warning is advisory; it does not pause or limit the run.
Turning workflows off also makes ultracode unavailable.

recall.q: What is the main difference between a workflow and subagents?
recall.a: The script holds the plan and intermediate results, not Claude.

recall.q: Can you answer questions during a run?
recall.a: No. Only permission prompts and usage-limit waits pause a run.

recall.q: How do you limit cost on a large job?
recall.a: Run it on a small slice first and watch per-agent usage in `/workflows`.
